title: AgentPS: Agentic Process Supervision for Content Moderation with Multimodal LLMs
measurement_description: The paper evaluated the model's ability to detect hate speech in multimodal social media posts (images and text) by incorporating process supervision. Specifically, it measured whether the model could correctly identify if an image and its accompanying text contain satirical, discriminatory, harmful, cursing, racial, or other hateful content directed toward a certain religion. This 'Religion score' was used as an intermediate reasoning step to improve the final hate speech classification.
findings: By decomposing complex content moderation into intermediate ancillary questions (including a specific evaluation for religious hate speech), the AgentPS model demonstrated significantly improved accuracy over vanilla models. For example, in a specific test case involving an antisemitic meme, the vanilla model failed to identify the hate speech (giving it a score of 0.034), whereas the AgentPS model correctly identified strong religious hate (Religion score of 0.959) and accurately classified the meme as hate speech (final score of 0.986).
